svg.title: MediBook normalized database schema
svg.desc: Three-table schema for patients, doctors, and appointments, with primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and one-to-many relationships.
svg.text: MediBook — Part A: normalized database schema
Exactly three entities • MySQL types • primary/foreign keys • business constraints shown

g.text: patients
People who book clinic appointments
patient_id BIGINT UNSIGNED PK, AI, NOT NULL
full_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL
email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, UNIQUE
phone VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
UQ: email
doctors
Clinic doctors and their consultation details
doctor_id BIGINT UNSIGNED PK, AI, NOT NULL
full_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL
specialty VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
consultation_fee DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL, CHECK (>= 0)
room VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
CK: consultation_fee >= 0
appointments
Booking plus retained cancellation and refund history
appointment_id BIGINT UNSIGNED PK, AI, NOT NULL
appointment_ref VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, UNIQUE
patient_id BIGINT UNSIGNED FK -> patients.patient_id, NOT NULL
doctor_id BIGINT UNSIGNED FK -> doctors.doctor_id, NOT NULL
appointment_datetime DATETIME NOT NULL
booked_at DATETIME NOT NULL, DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
amount_paid DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL, CHECK (>= 0)
status ENUM(confirmed,cancelled) NOT NULL, DEFAULT confirmed
cancelled_at DATETIME NULL
refund_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL, DEFAULT 0, CHECK (>= 0)
active_doctor_id BIGINT UNSIGNED GENERATED, NULLABLE
= doctor_id when confirmed; NULL when cancelled
Keys and constraints
PK: appointment_id • UQ: appointment_ref
FKs: patient_id and doctor_id; delete is RESTRICT
UQ(active_doctor_id, appointment_datetime): one active
appointment per doctor slot; cancelled rows have NULL key
CK: time is 09:00–16:30 on :00 or :30, zero seconds
CK: status/cancelled_at consistent; 0 <= refund <= amount_paid
Refund history stays on the cancelled appointment row.
The freed slot can be booked again because cancelled rows
do not participate in the active-slot unique key.
Where each rule is enforced
Database: NOT NULL / UNIQUE / CHECK constraints and foreign keys protect stored data.
Database concurrency: the active-slot unique key prevents two simultaneous bookings for the same doctor and time.
Transactional application logic: lock the doctor row while counting that day's active appointments; reject booking number 13.
Application validation: booking must be in the future. A CHECK constraint cannot safely compare with the moving current time.
Appointment status has only confirmed/cancelled; waitlist and notification queues live in Redis, not extra database entities.
Relationships: patients 1:N appointments • doctors 1:N appointments • every appointment has exactly one patient and one doctor.
